title: Scenario-based launch triage and KPI hypotheses
body:
Purpose:
A compact, scenario-driven checklist and KPI hypothesis sheet intended to guide the first 72 hours of a production feature launch for Redwood hosted inference routes. Focus: measurable gates, traffic shaping plans, quick triage play, and fallbacks. This is intentionally operational: short actions, owners, and abort criteria.

Audience:
Product ops, Release engineers, SRE on-call, Serving runtime eng, Console/product owners.

Scope:
- Applies to new API routes, model variant rollouts, or major perf-affecting infra releases (batching, kernel changes, quantization toggles).
- Not for routine patch releases unless they change runtime behavior or model weights.

Quick overview of scenarios (decision matrix):
1) Cold global launch (all regions receive traffic at start) — risk: spike to infra, cache cold misses
2) Staggered regional ramp (NA -> EU -> APAC) — risk: regional config drift, delayed observability
3) Canary traffic ramp (1% -> 10% -> 50%) — risk: regressions in quality, long-tail latency hits
4) Capacity-constrained fallback (route to cheaper model variant / lower-precision variant) — risk: quality regressions

KPI hypotheses (measured during ramps) — table rows as lines:
- KPI: P95 latency (in ms) | Hypothesis: will stay <= 220ms on p3-standard with autoscaling policy A | Instrument: per-route latency dashboard, token-level breakdown | Owner: SRE-Eng - Diego
- KPI: Cost per 1k tokens | Hypothesis: will reduce by 18% vs baseline when batching is enabled | Instrument: billing delta, per-request cost tags | Owner: Product Ops - Leah
- KPI: Quality regressions (eval set BLEU/ROUGE/LL delta) | Hypothesis: quantized variant will have <= 1.5% metric drift on eval suite | Instrument: eval delta alerts tied to prompt set `prod-gating-evals` | Owner: Applied ML - Priya
- KPI: Error rate (5xx by route) | Hypothesis: should not exceed 0.4% during ramp | Instrument: error budget dashboard, service logs sampling | Owner: Serving runtime - Omar
- KPI: Cold-start token throughput (tokens/sec) | Hypothesis: warm pools will hit target after 15m of steady traffic | Instrument: pool warmup metrics and KV cache hit rate | Owner: Release Eng - Diego

Traffic shaping & ramp plan (concrete numbers):
- Canary plan (default for major changes): 1% (T+0h), 5% (T+30m), 20% (T+2h), 50% (T+6h), 100% (T+24h). Pause at each step for verification window.
- Timebox for each step: 30m for early steps, 2h for mid steps, 24h soak after 100%.
- Regional rollout: NA start, wait 4h stability, then EU 25% -> 100% over 8h, then APAC 10% -> 100% over 12h.
- Emergency traffic cap: automatic policy to cap route at 30rps per-tenant if error rate > 0.8% for 10m.

Readiness checklist (pre-launch items - yes/no style):
- Autoscaling policy validated in staging and shadow test: [ ]
- Infra capacity reserve confirmed with cloud infra (committed Gpu pool): [ ]
- Model pinned and checksum verified in model registry: [ ]
- Canary runbook created and paged to on-call: [ ]
- Important dashboards and alert thresholds created (latency, error rate, cost delta): [ ]
- Rollback plan defined (route revert + model variant fallback) and tested in a dry-run: [ ]
- QA evals run on production-like data and results attached: [ ]
- Contract tests for SDK/console promotional UI validated: [ ]
- Privacy/compliance signoff for new data logging: [ ]

Operational playbook (if something goes wrong):
- Symptom: P95 latency spike > 300ms for 15m.
  - Immediate action: reduce traffic to 20% of current across all regions (Release Eng).
  - Next: spin additional dedicated capacity pool (SRE/Infra) and enable aggressive batching fallback policy.
  - If latency remains >300ms after 30m: rollback route to previous model variant and open urgent SEV-1.

- Symptom: Error rate > 1% for 10m.
  - Immediate action: divert 75% of traffic to fallback stable region/variant (SRE).
  - Next: capture 1 minute of full traces and sample requests for ML evaluation (Applied ML).
  - If persists -> rollback to previous canary or disable feature flag.

Abort criteria (explicit thresholds that trigger stop or rollback):
- Any of: sustained P95 > 350ms for 30m AND error rate > 0.8% -> abort ramp and rollback.
- Quality drift on eval suite > 3% on key metrics (LL delta or BLEU) -> abort and label as quality regression.
- Cost delta > 40% predicted and no mitigation path within 2h -> pause rollout and consult finance.

Telemetry & dashboards to monitor (minimum):
- Per-route latency (P50/P90/P95/P99), with token-level decomposition.
- Token cost per request and 1h rolling cost delta.
- Errors by code and by tenant, sampled full traces for new error spikes.
- KV cache hit rate and pool warmup status.
- Eval-run deltas mapped to prompt sets used in gating.

Owners & paging matrix (primary -> backup):
- Product Ops: Leah Kim -> Omar Torres
- Serving runtime: Omar Torres -> Diego Alvarez
- SRE/Infra: Diego Alvarez -> Viktor Smirnov
- Applied ML: Priya Nair -> Rachel Huang

Post-launch checks (T+24h, T+72h):
- T+24h: confirm metric stability, run targeted evals, annotate issues in the release ticket.
- T+72h: run cost analysis vs baseline, recommend permanent autoscale tuning or quantization profile changes.

Open questions / notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Do we want a separate traffic ramp policy for paid enterprise tenants vs self-serve? (pros/cons: SLA commitments)
- Investigate automatic conversion of console feature flag toggles into Jira tickets for auditability.
- Short test: add synthetic long-tail latency generator to staging for 3h to validate P99 behavior under load.

Attachments and quick links:
- Linked artifacts above include the canonical runbook and the Jira epic for the rollout.
- Quick command references: `infra/traffic-controller bump --route <r> --pct <n>` and `monitoring/alerts mute --route <r> --window 30m`.

Revision history (brief):
- 2025-11-08 created by Leah for internal pre-launch checklist experimentation.
- 2025-12-03 updated with canary numbers after SRE sim.
- 2026-02-20 added cost abort threshold and owner matrix.

End of sheet.
